title: Multi-lab replications convert single-effect claims into effect-size and boundary-condition maps
summary: Candidate pattern opened in rev0012: multi-lab replications should be represented as maps of effect size, uncertainty, protocol, sample, setting, and source-visibility constraints, not as binary gotcha verdicts. The pattern intentionally includes robust-control records alongside failures and shrinkage cases.

status_history.note: Promoted or created in rev0012 multi-lab replication / boundary-map pass.

claims.claim: Across Many Labs 1, Many Labs 2, RRRs, RP:CB, and ManyBabies, multi-lab replication turns single-study claims into estimates with lab/sample/protocol boundaries rather than simple true/false verdicts.
what_would_change_status: Future child records show these cases do not share enough structure to support a pattern.

claims.claim: The pattern’s practical query value is to ask not only “did it replicate?” but “under which protocol, population, lab ecology, materials, endpoints, and source-visibility constraints did the claim survive, shrink, fail, or remain unresolved?”
what_would_change_status: Users find the query grammar too broad or a better cross-record vocabulary replaces it.

evidence_profile.source_depth: pattern composed from promoted records, each one-pass source-backed
limitations: Psychology-heavy with one preclinical-cancer biology expansion.
evidence_profile.red_team_state: rev0016 scaffold added; controls not yet promoted

recurring_structure: outcome becomes map: robust, shrunk, weak, null-compatible, failed, or infeasible
non_equivalences: RRR single-protocol direct replication is not Many Labs multi-effect mapping
Cancer biology feasibility barriers are not psychology effect shrinkage
type_payload.guardrail: candidate only; do not use to declare a field invalid

positive_controls_needed: Add additional multi-lab efforts that convert a single-effect claim into an effect-size and boundary-condition map.
negative_controls_needed: Add multi-lab efforts with robust replication to avoid teaching that replication only means debunking.
counterexamples_to_seek: A case where multi-lab heterogeneity is mainly procedural drift rather than true boundary structure.
rollback_triggers: A second-review extraction demotes or materially weakens one of the support records.
A negative-control record shows the pattern label fits too many unrelated cases.
A counterexample shows the claimed recurrence is better explained by a narrower or different mechanism.
The pattern is upgraded only after controls and not by record count alone.
red_team_controls.split_or_merge_watch: Medium: failed direct replications, mixed boundary maps, robust controls, and project-completion barriers are distinct.

maturity_gate.minimum_before_mature: At least one positive control, at least one negative control, an explicit counterexample search, and a rollback/split decision recorded in the claim-status ledger.

handling_notes: Avoid turning replication into researcher humiliation or field dismissal.
Preserve the difference between failed, narrowed, inconclusive, and robust effects.
Do not promote clinical, educational, or policy implications beyond the source-backed record scope.

unknowns: No full child-record extraction of each original study, lab, dataset, and author response in this revision.
No local archived copy or full line-by-line source edition yet.
Future revisions should add post-RRR/meta-analytic status histories and field/practice lag checks.
next_actions: Create child records for each included original effect where source permanence and author-response materials justify it.
Add negative controls and successful controls from additional fields.
Separate direct replication, conceptual replication, reproducibility, and generalizability claims in later records.
Add at least one negative-control or counterexample record before upgrading this pattern beyond candidate level.
